title: Queue deconflict notes and morning ops checklist
content:
Quick context: morning brain‑dump for today's shift. Focus: reduce queue tail latency, finish the partial drain of pool-p-x, confirm nvlink anomalies aren't correlated with kernel upgrades. This is a personal checklist + notes-to-self, not an escalation doc.

Top priorities (order matters):
- Stabilize high-priority inference lane (lane: interactive-low-latency). Median p95 spiked to ~380ms overnight; investigate backlog and hot nodes.
- Finish draining pool-p-x GPUs for the maintenance window (nodemgr -> deprovision). Ensure live trace routing to fallback models while nodes are down.
- Confirm billed tagging for Dedicated test run (billing tags on newly added gpus were missing last month).

Immediate quick checks (first 15 mins):
- Query queue lengths: curl -s 'https://ops-api.internal/queues?lane=interactive-low-latency' | jq '.backlog, .p95' -> note numbers.
- SSH to node with highest tail latency (from console) and run: 
  - nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 10 -c 30
  - sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager | grep -i eviction
  - top -b -n1 | head -n20
- Check autoscaler decisions: kubectl get hpa -n inference -o wide | grep pool-p-x
- Quick health endpoints: cat /etc/redwood/agent.conf && curl -s http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep "kv_cache_hits"

Notes from yesterday's run (carry forward):
- evictions looked like preemptible behavior but nodes are not preemptible; likely kernel oom_killer nudges after 10:30UTC.
- One node (rack-9/node-12) had nvlink errors logged 3x between 03:14–03:38. Driver was 525.85; we rolled kernel to 6.1.19 last week.
- The cheap workaround: temporarily route interactive-small requests to quantized-2x model version to reduce GPU memory pressure while we rebalance.

Planned actions (this shift):
- 09:20: run rolling drain of pool-p-x with 10% concurrency: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120; watch queues and reroute if queue > 1500.
- 09:45: run perf-sample script on 3 worst nodes: scripts/perf-sample.sh --nodes rack-9/node-12,rack-3/node-4,rack-6/node-2 --duration 60s. Attach logs to JIRA-OPS-1427.
- 10:30: if nvlink logs persist, escalate to HW team and post snapshot to #infra-hardware with timestamp and nvidia-smi -q output.

Fallback and routing decisions:
- Policy: if p95>300ms for 2 consecutive checks (5m apart), instant route: interactive-low-latency -> interactive-fallback (same model family but smaller).
- If node failures >2 in same rack within 30m, enable cross-rack routing and limit batch size to 8 tokens per request for that lane.

Todo list (actionable items):
- [ ] Add missing billing tags to Dedicated test pool: tag:dedicated:env=test,owner=marcus (JIRA-OPS-1433).
- [ ] Update the drain playbook with pre-drain reroute step (small PR to infra/playbooks).
- [ ] Draft a short note for SRE weekly: "nvlink vs kernel — observations" (include log snippets).
- [ ] Recreate the p95 histogram from observability dashboard for the last 72h and export CSV.

Things to watch during the day (observability knobs):
- KV cache hit ratio per model: decline often correlates with sudden request amplifications.
- Token emission burst patterns: look for spikes in early tokens which signal aggressive sampling params upstream.
- GPU memory alloc failure counts (driver errors) — if >3 in 1h for the same node, schedule emergency cordon.

Commands and snippets I keep using:
- Check queue state (compact): curl -s 'https://ops-api.internal/queues?lane=interactive-low-latency' | jq '{backlog: .backlog, p95: .p95_ms}'
- Drain with graceful fallback tag: kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 && curl -XPOST https://ops-api.internal/routing/reroute -d '{"lane":"interactive-low-latency","fallback":"interactive-fallback"}'
- Capture nvlink logs: sudo dmesg | grep -i nvlink -n > /tmp/nvlink-$(date +%s).log

Open questions / decision notes:
- Is the kernel bump last week correlated? We saw small upticks across multiple racks but only this rack shows nvlink errors. Ask RE: did we change BIOS settings for power management during the last hardware ops? (ping Evan).
- Should we proactively increase the autoscaler target by 15% for interactive lane during major quantized promotions? Risk: cost spike vs reduced tail latency. Put a quick cost estimate in the PR.

Hand-off checklist (for next shift):
- Leave the CSV of p95 histograms and the perf-sample logs linked in the handoff message.
- Note which nodes were drained and their pre/post queue numbers.
- Explicitly state if fallback routing is still on (yes/no) and since what time.

Short retrospective bullets (post-shift to self):
- Keep a copy of the first nvlink log before any reboots (for HW).
- If billing tags are missing again, escalate to billing ops for an automated enforcement hook (prevent drift).

Snack-sized reminders to self (personal):
- Water bottle before the 10:30 check.
- Quick ping Priya about config change window, she usually replies with ETA.

If things go sideways (escalation path):
- Page oncall SRE -> mention JIRA-OPS-1427 and include sample traces.
- If >3 node failures in an hour, engage HW oncall and prepare to failover the entire lane to dedicated-fallback region (manual switch).

End of notes. Save and attach logs to JIRA-OPS-1427. Follow up: write the small playbook PR for pre-drain reroute before EOD.
